reviews.text: It's a certified trash game. Personally wasn't expecting much, except for a silly game about trash animals. What's advertised is what I got. Not too hard to decide whether it's for you or not. Don't dig too deep into it, unless you're looking for trash. Nothing extraordinary about the game, but it's cute and simple. The roguelike aspect is kinda funny due to the theme, but it's pretty smart in its presentation (eating trash, hell yeah). Story is trash, it's about trash. As they say, one man's trash is another man's treasure or something. Played a bit of the demo and the rogue stays overpowered. New character is nice for something fresh. Will definitely try to be more creative with how I play future runs (I wouldn't suggest nerfs but others should be tuned closer to the impact of the rogue). Overall, it's a trash game that's also kinda smelly.

That's a shame this game has a ton of potential and has a good core mechanic. I really wish they made this game work, but I'd wait until after early access to pick it up if at all. The balance is all over the place and it's a coin flip on if your first mission will lose the whole run once you get to the second area. I'll repost the review once I see the completed version, but I'm really worried about the chaos of all the random pieces turning this into a frustration engine. Between the luck of tetris pieces, luck of enemy spawn, and luck of loot generation, you really have no way to know if you're on your way to a complete loss. I've had runs where's it's been a steamroll because the tetris lined up an everyone had 20+ attack; I've had others where every battle was a grindstone struggle. I've never had a tough run turn into a win, however, and all too often a sure thing turns into a scrapped run because of bad luck. As mentioned, the worst offender is the first mission of the second zone where you have nothing but basics and the map can set itself up to that there's not any way to succeed (this can happen on any difficulty mode). The restart until you have a good run method works way better in fast-paced action style rogue-likes, and doing it in this game feels awful. I really want to like this game. I hope they figure out how to balance Rogue-Like and Tactics into something that is fun to play. There's so much potential here, and it was almost perfectly scratching a tactical itch I've had for some time. The frustration was just not worth it.

I really hate to vote this game down because for the most part, it's got a bit of charm, it's kinda fun and there is alot of potential there but in it's current state, it's my opinion that this whole game with the price tag - should have been the demo. I didn't try the demo so I don't know exactly whether it's more like a tutorial (which the game lacks but it is relatively intuitive) but the game only has 2 acts, the acts have 10 stages and these stages, for someone whose not totally new to this genre could be completed in about 5 minutes (per stage). The difficulty scales a touch but it's a very small touch. I tried playing this on Medium and found it not challenging. Now, there are harder level choices available but for Medium, that felt pretty easy. Even still, it's clear (you can check the achievements) that the content doesn't go beyond this point - so the idea of doing it all again just to hope for a slightly more challenging playthrough was not an appeal enough for me to redo it. I know this is early access and I get that someday this could be better. It's my hope that it does get better, I've played early access games before, these days its hard not to have stumbled across a few and I rarely request a refund but I had to for this game. It didn't feel right paying for it in it's current state. When I think of games this reminds me of, it has a rogue-like functionality where it has the character selection of say 'Dungeons of the Endless' but there are only 5 characters. It has a level progression system of a game like 'Slay the Spire'.. but there's only one path. There are 'boons' you can pick up like from 'Hades' -- but the options are very limited, reset in Act 2 and I ended up coming across an almost identical build without really trying. The grid like battle system reminds me of 'Final Fantasy Advance Tactics' but the options are so limited in its current form that it's not worth the price tag. I'm going to keep an eye on this one and if more content is released, I'll check it out, do some research and maybe buy it back. I like the game -- but it's not there yet to release it beyond a demo.

I'd call it "cute and compact", and if you like these short casual strat games you'll probably like this one too. The playthroughs are short, the maps are small, the art is charming, and the gameplay is simple. I would NOT call it deep though; there isn't much to it as far as I can tell. I wouldn't buy it unless youre prepared to get another game in about 10 hours. The biggest limitation to me is the lack of character customization options. Technically, you have a leveling system and an original trash-tetris style stat system, but in practice they don't really do the trick. The leveling system gives you a fixed drip of skills that you can pile onto one character, or spread out, but youre always just picking between two choices and you have to advance the characters within their intended build lanes, you cant change them. You dont even have enough control to focus on one character over another, because you get two choices FROM AMONG THE WHOLE PARTY, and only once or twice per level. At most you can level half your party, and if your luck is bad you can go levels without getting the animal you want to improve. You can go an entire run, without seeing the skill you want to get, or see it one fight before the run is over. The stat system WAS fun, because eating trash tetris and finding tunafish cans that give you stats is really cool, but it shifts your attention from stat building to clearing lines efficiently, and I always just ended up with roughly even stats on everyone. By the end, everyone has about 70-90hp, everyone has about 3 or 4 mp/turn, we all have enough mana to use all our skills comfortably... movement is extremely limited in the first few stages, but by stage four or five, I forgot it was a stat; I always have extra movement after the first two rounds. Also, the short runs meant i had to keep dropping my level progress and start over on each new stage. There were 10 stages in each of the acts I played so far, and each time the progression went: were slow and tougher than the enemy --> now were moderately powerful and faster --> were overpowered and maybe one fight will be hard --> the run is already over --> all my characters get wiped and i have to start new ones --> :( All of the characters I have unlocked so far have been fun and unique, and the atmosphere of the game is great. Good art, good vibe. I actually really would love this game, if I had more control over my characters and more time to explore their builds. Its really fallen out of favor these days to present the player with a character sheet and let them pick stats and skills, but that's what i would have loved in this game. I recommend it as a casual dip that you'll play for a few hours. I cant imagine anyone getting three digit playtimes out of this. I have enjoyed it, but i don't feel very challenged or hooked and Im already ready to move on.
